# dsh-terminal-shell
English | 中文
On Windows, choose which shell sits behind the terminal tool the agent invokes — **PowerShell** (`pw
sh`), the **local Git Bash** (`bash`), or **`cmd.exe`** (`cmd`). One switch under **Settings → Gener
al**, applied to **new sessions only**: no preset file edited, no global `ctx.shell` takeover.
`v0.2.1` · MIT · Windows (DSH Desktop / Web shell) · `engines.node` `>=22` · `engines.dsh` `>=0.2.1-
IT · Windows (DSH Desktop / Web shell) · `engines.node` `>=22` · `engines.dsh` `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0`
## Why this plugin
DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 ships **one** terminal per platform, and on Windows that is PowerShell: the bash fami
ly is disabled by `!!js process.platform === 'win32'` assertions in `dsh-base`, and `ctx.shell` is a
**single-instance** service (a second registration throws `service "shell" has been registered`). A
Windows session therefore has no bash executor and no `bash` tool.
The common ways to change that each cost something:
| Approach | Cost / limitation |
| Patch the platform assertion in `dsh-base` or the profile | Edits first-party composition; affects

one plane only; needs a restart |
| Write your own PTY / tool from scratch | Re-implements a 60 KB+

tool contract; drifts from official behavior |
| Drop in a **global** shell replacer | Changes **ev
ery** session, even ones that never asked; collides with the host executor |
**This plugin does per-session isolated replacement instead** — that is its point:
- **Only new sessions, and only the ones you switch.** The executor is composed into each new sessio
n's own `isolate('shell')` subtree; the host plane and all other sessions stay untouched, and uninst

alling leaves no residue.
- **Three dialects, one switch, and install changes nothing.** `dialect` d

efaults to `pwsh`, so out of the box behavior is identical to the official one.
- **No pinned execut
able paths.** Git Bash is discovered at runtime on each machine, so the same repo works everywhere.
- **Covers the sidebar too.** An extra option makes the sidebar **New Terminal → Shell** menu launch
this machine's Git Bash instead of WSL's `bash` — something the stock menu cannot do.
Beyond Git Bash, the **`cmd`** dialect is there for when you want Windows-native behavior instead of
a POSIX layer: exact `cmd.exe` batch semantics (`.cmd` scripts, `%VAR%` expansion, native pipes and
redirection) with no MSYS dependency. It is a one-shot executor reusing the official tool contract,
so the model can drive plain `cmd` exactly as the OS runs it.
[该节后续省略]
### How it works
On `agent/created`, the plugin composes everything into the new session only:

`restrict` only hides the *inherited* layer, so it removes the preset's `pwsh` without touching the
`bash` this layer registered (`cmd` denies `pwsh` + `bash`). All steps are released in reverse when
the session ends, and a mid-way failure rolls back. New sessions only — tool catalogs are assembled
at session creation and cannot be swapped at runtime.
> The **Terminal shell** row (bash dialect). The highlighted last line, **Sidebar terminal**, is the
option that makes the sidebar New Terminal use this machine's Git Bash.
## Install / enable
**Prerequisites:** Windows; DSH Desktop / Web shell `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0`; for `bash` a local Git fo
r Windows / MSYS2 / Cygwin; for `cmd` nothing extra.
Install it like any other profile plugin — either way works:
- **In the app:** open **Plugins → Add plugin**, paste the package name `dsh-terminal-shell` (or thi

s repository's URL, or a local folder path), click **Install**, then **Enable now**.
- **CLI:** `dsh
plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-terminal-shell` — it runs pnpm inside the profile and registers
the bundle automatically. A GitHub URL or a local path works too.
The package ships its own `dsh.bundle.patch`, which inserts exactly one row and pins no executable p

**Restart DSH after install or upgrade** — a row inserted at runtime only enters the composition tre
e; `apply` is not called until restart. `dialect` stays `pwsh` until you change it.
## Known limitations
### cmd dialect limitations
`cmd` is the only dialect **not** built on the official bash tool (`src/cmd/tool.ts` is a verbatim p
ort); every constraint below comes from `cmd.exe` / batch semantics:
1. **One-shot batch** — each call is a fresh temporary `.cmd`; `pause`, `set /p`, or any interactive

prompt hangs until timeout.
2. **No echo** — `cmd.exe /q` disables command echo, so only the comman

d's own output returns; `@echo on` cannot override `/q`.
3. **Batch placeholders** — `%0` / `%1`–`%9
` / `%*` / `%~dp0` point at the plugin's internal script, not your command line; use `%CD%` for the

working directory.
4. **`%VAR%` expands per batch rules** — a `set` on the same line is not visible

to a new variable on that line.
5. **Encoding** — non-ASCII output depends on the console code page

(`cmdCodePage`, default `65001`).
6. **`cmdPath` only accepts `cmd.exe`** — anything else is rejecte
d by the client and by discovery; empty falls back to `%ComSpec%` → `%SystemRoot%\System32\cmd.exe`.
7. **No persistent PTY** — `cmd` has no persistent terminal and does not replace `minimal`'s persis

tent shell.
8. **Sandbox-denied marker may be missing** — on Chinese Windows the denial message is G
BK, so the provider's English signatures may not match; the sandbox still applies and the plugin doe
s not fake the verdict.
Each execution writes a `cmd-<uuid>.cmd` into the executor's own scratch dir (cwd set to that dir, i
nvoked by bare name) because `cmd.exe` cannot take a quoting-safe multi-line command as an argument;
a `cd /d "<cwd>"` guard prevents silently running in the scratch dir, and the script's exit code is
left as the last command's own.
## Compatibility
Windows only (`disabled: !!js process.platform !== 'win32'`). DSH Desktop / Web shell. `engines.node
>=22`, `engines.dsh >=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0`. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm` is a `peerDependency`, external at
build time. Coexists with a persistent-terminal bundle (e.g. `experimental-terminal-bundle`): the t
wo registries and `terminal_*` tools never read or write each other's state.
